Reading shouldSnapshot and the compaction helpers shows that a node whose log store has been emptied while its snapshot index is high (which compaction after a snapshot install or a user restore does produce) computes an underflowed delta. This turn records that as a sourced question with a precise discriminator; it is not yet executed, so the interpretation stays source-only.

investigations.question: Can a node whose log store was emptied while its last snapshot index is higher report that it should take a snapshot even though no new entry has been committed since that snapshot, and what is the observable consequence?
investigations.hypothesis: shouldSnapshot computes delta as the unsigned difference between the log store's last index and the cached last snapshot index; when the store's last index is below the snapshot index the subtraction underflows to a very large value, so the threshold test passes and the node attempts a snapshot it does not need.
investigations.discriminator: Drive a real node to the state where the log store is empty and the snapshot index is high (a follower that installs a snapshot and compacts its logs, or a leader that completes a user restore with a non-monotonic log store), then call shouldSnapshot and takeSnapshot and compare against a control node whose store still holds entries past the snapshot: the underflowed node must report true and attempt a snapshot at the unchanged index while the control reports the threshold verdict, and the FSM's applied index must be unchanged in both.

interpretations.rationale: Source-only account. shouldSnapshot reads the log store's LastIndex and the cached last snapshot index and returns delta >= SnapshotThreshold, with delta computed as an unsigned subtraction. compactLogsWithTrailing deletes everything up to min(snapIdx, lastLogIdx-trailingLogs), and both the snapshot-install path and the user-restore path set the snapshot index to at least the installed index while the log store keeps only newer entries; on a log store that tolerates gaps this can leave LastIndex below the snapshot index, so the subtraction underflows instead of being negative. The account therefore predicts a spurious positive verdict rather than a missed snapshot. I am not asserting a defect: the consequence I can source is limited to an extra snapshot attempt at an unchanged index, and whether that matters depends on consumer expectations for SnapshotThreshold that this snapshot does not settle.
limitations: Source-only: the underflow is derived from reading the arithmetic and the compaction callers, not observed; no retained execution yet shows the emptied-store state.
The consequence is bounded to snapshot scheduling; nothing in this reading shows loss of committed entries or a change to which entries are applied, so it should not be read as a safety claim.

The reachable variant depends on which SnapshotStore and LogStore are in use (monotonic stores remove all logs, gap-tolerant stores compact up to the snapshot), and neither variant has been exercised here.
